key_insight: The paper argues that anomaly and feature selection should be optimized jointly under fixed budgets, because feature-first ranking can miss interactions and becomes more sensitive to calibration error as the number of selected samples grows.
engineering_relevance: Coupling-Grouped XY-QAOA shows a hardware-aware way to run constraint-preserving bipartite-selection QAOA at larger widths and depths on IBM Heron R3 while reducing circuit cost.
method: Formulate joint sample-feature selection as a fixed-budget constrained optimization problem.
Use a grouped-angle XY-QAOA variant that preserves feasibility during mixing.
Apply hardware-aware transpilation and warm-start/repair strategies to improve feasible output quality.
evidence_signal: On matched sparse IBM Heron R3 benchmarks, the implementation cut depth by 45.9%-61.3% and two-qubit gates by 2.6%-5.2%, achieved 64 qubits at p=2 and 36 qubits at p=3, and in 20-qubit p=5 runs retained 63% valid samples.
watch_item: Performance depends on sparse benchmark structure and hardware-aware compilation, so gains may not transfer directly to denser problems or different quantum devices.
paper_title: Coupling-Grouped XY-QAOA for Joint Anomaly-Feature Selection
